narrative.title: The Paging Ticket Dispenser for a Sorted Archive
narrative.scenario: An audit terminal must stream a sorted archive one record at a time without ever loading it all into memory. The dispenser keeps only the leftmost unvisited spine of the filing tree on a small stack: each 'next' pops the smallest pending record and quietly loads that record's right wing's spine for later. 'hasNext' just peeks whether any spine remains.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and a list of calls, each 'next' or 'hasNext'. The first call sequence starts after initialization.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the list of results for the calls in order — an integer for each 'next' and a boolean for each 'hasNext'.
constraints: next() and hasNext() run in amortized O(1); the stack may hold O(h) nodes
All calls are legal: next() is never called when hasNext() is false

testCases.explanation: The dispenser streams the inorder sequence 3, 7, 9, 15, 20 and then runs dry.
A one-node archive yields its single record and immediately reports exhaustion.

hintLevels: Level 1: You need sorted output on demand without flattening the tree up front.
Level 2: A stack of the leftmost spine simulates the recursion — pop the smallest, then seed the stack from its right child.
Level 3: Amortized O(1): every node is pushed and popped exactly once across the whole iteration.
